title: Signature Level Descent — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Hierarchical navigation treats the archive as a tree — network, archive, database, collection, record, element — and moves down it one level at a time, resolving each step before taking the next. At every level the engine lists the children, filters them by the objective, and descends into the most promising branch. If a branch proves empty, it backtracks exactly one level and tries the next candidate, so no effort is wasted re-walking good ground. This disciplined descent is how a search stays oriented inside billions of records. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
demo:
TREE = {"net": ["arch1", "arch2"], "arch1": ["db1", "db2"],
        "db1": ["coll1"], "coll1": ["rec1", "rec2"]}
def descend(path, target):
    node = path[-1]
    print("at", "/".join(path))
    if node == target: return path
    for child in TREE.get(node, []):
        r = descend(path + [child], target)
        if r: return r
    return None
print("found:", descend(["net"], "rec2"))

title: Signature Breadcrumb Backtracking — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Every descent leaves breadcrumbs — the ordered list of levels visited — so the engine always knows how it got somewhere and can retrace its steps. Backtracking pops the most recent level and resumes from the next unexplored sibling, which guarantees systematic coverage without bookkeeping errors. Breadcrumbs are also shown to the user as a navigable trail, turning an opaque machine walk into an understandable journey. Any hierarchical navigator that cannot say where it has been cannot be trusted about where it is going. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
demo:
trail = ["net", "arch1", "db1"]
print("trail:", " > ".join(trail))
trail.pop()
print("backtrack to:", " > ".join(trail))
trail.append("db2")
print("try sibling:", " > ".join(trail))

title: Signature Faceted Drill-Down — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Instead of guessing which branch to descend, faceted drill-down shows the value distribution at each level — years, topics, formats — and lets the objective pick the facet values that matter. Selecting a facet value prunes every branch that cannot contain it, often eliminating most of the tree in one step. Facets are computed from samples when full scans are too slow, with counts marked as estimates. This turns navigation from blind walking into informed elimination. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.

title: Signature Zoom Resolution — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. A hierarchical path like archive/db/collection/record is a promise that must be resolved level by level, verifying each segment exists before descending into it. Zoom resolution walks the path, and the moment a segment fails it reports the deepest valid prefix instead of a bare error. Partial resolution still has value: knowing the collection exists but the record does not is actionable information. This careful, verifying descent is what makes deep links into huge archives reliable. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.

title: Signature Ancestor Traversal — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Sometimes the record is found but its meaning lives above it — the collection's description, the database's provenance, the archive's access policy. Ancestor traversal walks back up the hierarchy collecting context at each level, so the leaf record arrives with its full lineage attached. Context is inherited downward but can be overridden at lower levels, exactly like scope in programming languages. A navigator that only returns leaves without their ancestors returns facts without their meaning. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
provenance: JAH Databases archive-intelligence tools program, lane T2a — Signature original authored for Justin Addam Higgins.
